claims.text: Torres and Loureiro’s 2015 documentary edition identifies Lisbon men recruited for the Ceuta fleet on 8 July 1415 and grain/legume tax relief on 6 December because fleet preparations depleted Lisbon. The Spanish Army Museum separately dates Fernando III’s Seville siege from August 1247 to 23 November 1248. These are expansion logistics and conquest, not the dates of charter confirmation.

claims.text: The 1415 fleet event concerns Portuguese expansion via Lisbon, not Lisbon’s conquest. Original dated manuscripts remain uncollated; the Portuguese edition and Spanish military museum retrospective are mediated. Siege and tax relief are distinct acts, not popular consent. Lisbon 1147 is not selected; no out-of-period conquest or unbroken expansion inferred.

claims.text: Lisbon’s catalogue identifies Afonso II’s confirmation of an earlier foral; its date differs from a separate archive guide. Seville’s exhibition identifies later confirmations, fairs and a specified mills-for-water obligation. A royal grant does not give both cities identical duties. These custodial descriptions leave original clauses uncollated and do not establish universal municipal rights. Separately, the edition links Lisbon’s 1415 fleet preparations to Ceuta and tax relief; the museum dates Seville’s siege to 1247–48. These expansion acts are not charter confirmations.

options: The Seville mills’ duty to supply the Alcázar and two fountains.
